summary: Named the 5 human-decided stack components (CRM API Service, CRM Web App, Structured Data Store, Vector Store, NLU/Extraction & Q&A Layer), each with a stated responsibility and non-responsibility, and clarified that the PRD's 5 named 'agents' are logical capability modules inside the single backend component (CRM API Service), not separate services -- the human-decided stack names one backend, not five. Documented system context and call/data flow (all crossings synchronous; no queue/worker component exists in the declared stack). Recorded 9 technology-compatibility decisions (SOL-1..SOL-9): 7 proposed (backend topology, web-API protocol, NLU invocation pattern, FastAPI rationale, React rationale, embedding-source integration point, vector/NLU access boundary) and 2 fixed-upstream (SQLite, Chroma -- rationale recorded, not re-decided). Traced all 21 stories across all 7 features to components, with operation_ids/entity_names marked not_applicable throughout since data_integration has not run yet. Found and disclosed a real hash discrepancy on the upstream PRD file (current CRLF bytes hash differently than the LF bytes Workflow 1's lock recorded against) -- verified content-identical after line-ending normalization, recorded as non-blocking Open Item OI-1 rather than silently resolved.

source_references.note: Workflow 1's own workflow.json, confirming its locked status at the moment this discipline read it. Backfilled by the coordinator after check-artifacts required a third source_reference entry the drafting agent had not written.

Disclosed as Open Item OI-1 in the document rather than silently using either hash.

decisions.choice: Single modular-monolith CRM API Service (FastAPI) containing five logical capability modules (Capture, Extraction, Memory/Q&A, Commitment Tracking, Brief-Me) plus an adapter layer, rather than one microservice per PRD 'agent'.
alternatives: One microservice per PRD agent (5 backend services)
decisions.rationale: stack.components[] names exactly one backend component with implemented_by: backend -- the human decision already fixed the deployment grain. Splitting into 5 services adds inter-service network calls and cross-service consistency risk against a single SQLite file, with no PRD/Stories requirement driving it for this single-persona, single-shared-login demo.

decisions.choice: Synchronous REST/JSON over HTTPS between CRM Web App and CRM API Service.
decisions.rationale: Every PRD/Stories AC for capture, Q&A, and brief requests is phrased as one-shot request/response with no NFR calling for streaming or partial responses. FastAPI's OpenAPI generation from REST/JSON directly feeds data_integration's contract work.

decisions.choice: Every call from CRM API Service to the NLU/Extraction & Q&A Layer happens synchronously in-request; no message broker or background-worker component exists.
alternatives: Asynchronous background processing with a task queue/worker and a polled status
decisions.rationale: stack.components[] declares no queue/broker/worker component; F-6 AC2 requires a newly captured note to appear automatically without further rep action, consistent with immediate synchronous consistency rather than a pending state. No NFR states a response-time budget forcing offload.
decisions.source: stack.components[] (no queue/worker entry); PRD F-6 AC2

decisions.choice: Python (FastAPI) for the backend, confirmed coherent with the NLU and vector-store technologies.
decisions.rationale: Both boto3 (AWS/Bedrock) and chromadb (Chroma) are first-class Python libraries; keeping the backend in Python avoids splitting extraction/retrieval logic across languages. FastAPI's async I/O suits the mostly I/O-bound calls to Bedrock/Chroma/SQLite, and its OpenAPI generation gives data_integration a machine-checkable contract starting point.
decisions.source: stack.components[] (backend = Python (FastAPI)); NLU/vector store's own declared technologies

decisions.choice: React (web SPA) for the frontend, confirmed coherent with the backend/protocol choices.
decisions.rationale: F-6 AC2's 'appear automatically' and F-7's identical-content-across-sessions requirements are naturally served by an SPA re-fetching client-side state rather than full-page reloads. React's ecosystem tools well against an OpenAPI-described REST backend, easing the Workflow 3 frontend build.
decisions.source: stack.components[] (frontend = React (web SPA)); PRD F-6 AC2, F-7

decisions.choice: AWS Bedrock (NLU/Extraction & Q&A Layer) is the sole source of embeddings stored in Chroma (Vector Store); no separate embedding-model provider is introduced.
alternatives: A dedicated third-party/local embedding model distinct from the LLM provider
decisions.rationale: PRD Assumption 10 leaves the specific embedding model open but already fixed the NLU/LLM technology as Bedrock. Sourcing embeddings from the same already-declared component avoids a sixth technology dependency purely for embeddings. Does not resolve which specific Bedrock embedding model, dimension, or re-embedding trigger -- left to data_integration (Open Item OI-1a).

decisions.choice: Vector Store and NLU/Extraction & Q&A Layer are reachable only from CRM API Service; CRM Web App never calls either directly.
alternatives: Allowing CRM Web App to call the NLU layer directly for perceived Q&A latency savings
decisions.rationale: Keeps every cross-cutting concern (matching, retrieval composition, synthesis) inside the one backend component, avoiding duplicated business logic client-side and giving security_nfr a single boundary to reason about.

decisions.choice: SQLite for the Structured Data Store.
alternatives: Not weighed by this discipline -- fixed directly by human decision at Requirements Gate 2
decisions.rationale: Self-contained, serverless, file-based engine consistent with the no-budget-ceiling demo scope; fully compatible with the Python/FastAPI backend (stdlib sqlite3 driver, no separate service). Compatibility constraint not yet resolved: SQLite's single-writer-at-a-time behavior is in tension with F-7/US-21's concurrent-write requirement (Open Item OI-2).

decisions.choice: Chroma (with semantic chunking) for the Vector Store.
alternatives: Not weighed by this discipline -- fixed directly by human decision at Requirements Gate 2
decisions.rationale: Chroma ships a first-class Python client (chromadb), consistent with the Python/FastAPI backend. Can run embedded or as a lightweight local server for this demo's scope; exact deployment mode left to platform.

acceptance_criteria: The system must create a structured interaction note and associate it with the correct customer thread when the rep's typed entry unambiguously matches exactly one seeded customer account.
The system must save the entry as a new interaction note when the entry contains at least one non-whitespace character.
verification_scenarios: Type a one-line note unambiguously naming exactly one seeded account; confirm a new interaction record is created and thread-tagged to that account.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; neither exists yet -- solution is the first discipline in this workflow.

acceptance_criteria: The system must reject the submission with an explicit 'cannot save an empty note' message, and must not create any note record, when the rep submits an empty or whitespace-only entry.

The system must flag the note as 'unmatched — needs customer selection' — rather than attaching it to a default or incorrect account — when no seeded customer account can be unambiguously identified from the entry text.
verification_scenarios: Submit a whitespace-only entry, confirm rejection with no record created.
Submit an entry naming no/an ambiguous account, confirm 'unmatched' flag rather than default attachment.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; not yet drafted.

acceptance_criteria: The system must attach a previously flagged 'unmatched' note to the customer thread the rep selects when the rep manually resolves the flag.
The system must leave the note in the unmatched/needs-selection state — rather than guessing an account — when the rep has not yet resolved it.
verification_scenarios: Resolve an unmatched note to a selected customer; confirm re-tag.
Confirm an unresolved unmatched note is never auto-assigned.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; not yet drafted.

acceptance_criteria: [INFERRED — needs confirmation] The system must extract the contact's name, company and role from a scanned business-card image into the structured interaction note when the image is legible and contains recognizable contact fields. The OCR mechanism was never discussed in discovery (PRD Assumption 5, Open Question 5); whether this is worth building for the demo at all is still open.
[INFERRED — needs confirmation] The system must inform the rep that manual entry is required — without fabricating contact details — when the image cannot be read or no contact fields are recognized.
verification_scenarios: Submit a legible business-card image, confirm structured contact fields populate.
Submit an unreadable image, confirm manual-entry prompt with no fabricated fields.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; not yet drafted. See OI-3 (OCR technology sufficiency).

acceptance_criteria: The system must extract every distinct attendee name mentioned in a typed free-text interaction entry as a separate structured attendee item — recording one item per distinct person named (e.g., 'met Priya and Arjun from Acme...' must yield two attendee items, not one merged string) — when the entry text names at least one identifiable person.
The system must record zero attendee items for that interaction — rather than fabricating a name — when the entry text names no one.

[INFERRED — needs confirmation] The exact name-recognition/disambiguation mechanism was never discussed in discovery (PRD Assumption 14, Open Question 15); only the underlying capability (AC1/AC2) is treated as confirmed.
verification_scenarios: Submit the canonical 'met Priya and Arjun from Acme' example; confirm two distinct attendee rows.
Submit an entry naming no one; confirm zero attendee rows.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; not yet drafted. See OI-4 (mechanism inference).

acceptance_criteria: The system must extract each distinct commitment, follow-up or next step mentioned in a captured note's text as a separate tracked item when the note contains one or more of them.
The system must record no commitment items when the note describes discussion only, with no forward-looking commitment.
verification_scenarios: Submit a note with two distinct commitments; confirm two tracked items.
Submit a discussion-only note; confirm zero commitment items.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; not yet drafted.

acceptance_criteria: The system must record a due date on an extracted commitment when the captured text states a concrete date or an unambiguous relative date term resolvable against the interaction's timestamp (e.g., 'by Friday').

The system must mark the commitment's due date as unspecified — rather than guessing a date — when the text uses a vague temporal reference (e.g., 'soon,' 'sometime') or gives no date information at all.
verification_scenarios: Submit a commitment with 'by Friday'; confirm resolved due date.
Submit one with 'soon'; confirm due date recorded as unspecified.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; not yet drafted.

acceptance_criteria: The system must tag every extracted discussion point and commitment to the same customer thread as its source interaction note when that note is matched to a thread.
The system must flag an extracted item for manual thread assignment — rather than tagging it to an incorrect thread — when the source note itself is unmatched to a customer thread (per F-1).
verification_scenarios: Confirm extracted items on a matched note land on the same thread.
Confirm extracted items on an unmatched note are held for manual assignment.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; not yet drafted.

acceptance_criteria: The system must answer a natural-language question about a customer's most recent discussion by returning content drawn from that customer's most recent interaction note(s) when the thread has at least one captured note.
The system must respond that no history exists yet for that customer when the thread is empty.
verification_scenarios: Ask 'what did we discuss last time' against a thread with history; confirm answer drawn from that thread.
Ask against an empty thread; confirm explicit 'no history yet'.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; not yet drafted.

acceptance_criteria: The system must answer a natural-language question about the rep's own open commitments for a customer by listing the commitments extracted and tagged to that thread when any exist.
The system must state that there are no open commitments for that customer when none exist.
verification_scenarios: Ask about open commitments against a thread with commitments; confirm list matches tagged commitments.
Ask against a thread with none; confirm explicit empty response.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; not yet drafted.

acceptance_criteria: The system must answer a natural-language question about interaction attendees by returning the contact names extracted from that thread's interaction notes when attendee names were captured.
The system must state that no attendee information was captured when none was extracted.
verification_scenarios: Ask who attended against a thread with captured attendees; confirm names match F-1 AC5 output.
Ask against a thread with none; confirm explicit empty response.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; not yet drafted.

acceptance_criteria: The system must resolve and answer against the correct customer thread when a query names exactly one customer that matches a seeded account.
The system must respond that it could not identify the customer — rather than guessing or returning another customer's data — when the query names no customer or an unrecognized one.
verification_scenarios: Ask a question naming exactly one seeded account; confirm correct thread answers.
Ask one naming no/unrecognized customer; confirm explicit 'could not identify' response.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; not yet drafted.

acceptance_criteria: The system must list every open commitment whose due date has passed as 'overdue' when the current date is past that due date, and must exclude a commitment from this list once it is marked complete.

[INFERRED — needs confirmation] The system must list every open commitment whose due date falls within the next 7 days as 'due soon,' and must reclassify it as 'overdue' instead once its due date has passed. The 7-day window is a carried-over illustrative placeholder from the PRD, not a confirmed value (PRD Open Question 6).

The system must list a commitment with an unspecified due date (per F-2) separately from the due-soon/overdue list — rather than omitting it entirely or treating it as overdue — when no due date was captured.
verification_scenarios: Seed commitments past due, within 7 days, beyond 7 days, and with no due date; confirm each classifies correctly on a known reference date. No NLU call in this flow.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; not yet drafted.

acceptance_criteria: The system must state explicitly that there are no due-soon or overdue commitments — rather than showing an empty list with no explanation — when none exist.
verification_scenarios: Query the list when no commitment qualifies; confirm explicit 'none' message rather than silent empty list.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; not yet drafted.

acceptance_criteria: The system must generate a summary containing recent discussion history, open commitments and stakeholder/contact names for a named customer when that customer has at least one captured note, and must state that no history exists yet for that customer — rather than generating a summary with fabricated content — when the thread is empty.

[INFERRED — needs confirmation] The system must return a bounded, short-form summary (a few sentences or bullets, not a multi-page document) under normal conditions, and must still return whatever partial content is available, rather than failing the whole request, when data for one of the summary components is missing (PRD Open Question 7).
verification_scenarios: Request a brief for a customer with history; confirm summary combines structured + semantically-retrieved content and remains short-form.
Request a brief for an empty thread; confirm explicit no-history response.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; not yet drafted.

acceptance_criteria: [INFERRED — needs confirmation] The system must synthesize the opportunity/deal-status component narratively from that customer's recorded interaction notes and commitments — since no discrete deal-stage field exists in the structured store — when the thread contains content indicating where the deal/opportunity stands (PRD Assumption 13, Open Question 14).
The system must state that no opportunity/deal-status information has been captured yet for that customer — rather than fabricating a stage or outcome — when the thread contains no such content.
verification_scenarios: Request a brief for a customer whose notes discuss deal progress; confirm narrative synthesis draws only from existing content.
Request one with no such content; confirm explicit 'not captured' response.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; not yet drafted. Depends on data_integration ratifying no new deal-stage entity (PRD Section 13.1).

acceptance_criteria: The system must generate the summary for a named customer when the request unambiguously identifies exactly one seeded customer account.
The system must respond that it could not identify the requested customer — rather than guessing — when the request names an unrecognized or ambiguous customer.
verification_scenarios: Request a brief naming exactly one seeded account; confirm it generates.
Request one naming an ambiguous/unrecognized account; confirm explicit rejection.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; not yet drafted.

acceptance_criteria: The system must display a customer's captured notes and extracted items in chronological order on that customer's profile view when at least one note exists.
The system must display an explicit 'no history yet' state when none exists.
verification_scenarios: Open a profile with captured notes; confirm chronological ordering.
Open one with none; confirm explicit empty state.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; not yet drafted.

acceptance_criteria: The system must display a newly captured note and its extracted items on the correct customer's profile view automatically, without requiring the rep to take further action, when the note is tagged to that customer's thread.
The system must not display that note or its items on any other customer's profile view when it is not tagged to that customer.
verification_scenarios: Capture a note, then reopen that customer's profile; confirm it appears without extra action.
Confirm it does not appear on a different customer's profile.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; not yet drafted.

acceptance_criteria: The system must show the same customer thread content to every session authenticated via the shared login when two sessions view the same customer.
The system must not partition data by which physical person is at the keyboard, since no per-rep identity exists in this version.
verification_scenarios: Open the same customer in two sessions under the shared login; confirm identical content, no per-session partitioning.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; not yet drafted.

acceptance_criteria: [INFERRED — needs confirmation] The system must persist a note added from one session so that it is immediately visible to another concurrent session viewing the same customer thread. The conflict-handling mechanism was never discussed in discovery (PRD Open Question 9).
[INFERRED — needs confirmation] The system must not silently lose one session's addition when another session adds to the same thread at nearly the same time.
verification_scenarios: Add notes from two sessions to the same thread at nearly the same time; confirm both persist as distinct records.
traceability.not_applicable: data_integration owns the API contract and data model; not yet drafted. See OI-2 (SQLite concurrent-writer behavior).

open_items.detail: The specific Bedrock embedding model, its vector dimension, and the re-embedding trigger strategy (PRD Assumption 10) remain unconfirmed. SOL-6 fixes which component supplies embeddings; it does not fix which model.
